findings.location: (first paragraph, list of negative words)
findings.source_quote: It appears rather coincidental that so many words with a negative connotation begin with the letter D: Disappointment, Doubt, Doleful, Doom, Disillusionment, Discouragement, Dreary, Defeat, Despondency, Depression, Despair, Devastation, Deception, and Death.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate each English word into accurate, negative-connotation Afrikaans equivalents, preserving the list and order. Example correction (preserve the HTML and punctuation): “Dit blyk toevallig te wees dat soveel woorde met ’n negatiewe konnotasie met die letter D begin: Teleurstelling, Twyfel, Droefheid, Onheil, Onttovering, Ontmoediging, Sombêrheid, Nederlaag, Wanhoop, Depressie, Moedeloosheid, Verwoesting, Bedrog, en Dood.” Adjust wording if you prefer different conventional Afrikaans synonyms, but ensure meanings match the printed English words (Disillusionment → Onttovering or Ontsluiting/Verblinding-omkering; Dreary → Sombêrheid; Doom → Onheil).
findings.translation_quote: Dit lyk nogal toevallig dat soveel woorde met ’n negatiewe konnotasie met die letter D begin: Teleurstelling, Twyfel, Droefheid, Dood, Ontwaking, Ontmoediging, Duiwelagtig, Nederlaag, Hopeloosheid, Depressie, Wanhoop, Verwoesting, Bedrog, en Dood.

findings.location: Paragraph: “The road from Jerusalem to Emmaus was about threescore furlongs…”
findings.source_quote: The road from Jerusalem to Emmaus was about threescore furlongs or approximately seven miles.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the original measurement wording and render it accurately into Afrikaans. For example: “Die pad vanaf Jerusalem na Emmaus was ongeveer threescore furlongs (ongeveer sewe myl).” Or translate the historical unit into a conventional Afrikaans equivalent plus the explanatory miles in parentheses. Avoid substituting a different ancient unit that changes the numeric meaning (the translation currently says ‘ongeveer dertig stadiën’, which does not match ‘threescore furlongs’).
findings.translation_quote: Die pad vanaf Jerusalem na Emmaus was ongeveer dertig stadiën of ongeveer sewe myl.

findings.location: Sentence: “they overcame the initial defenses and swarmed into the German-held territory.”
findings.source_quote: After several months of intense fighting, they overcame the initial defenses and swarmed into the German-held territory.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the awkward or erroneous Afrikaans phrase. Replace “het in die deur die Duitse gebied ingestorm” with a clear equivalent: “het die aanvanklike verdediging oorkom en in die deur ŉ uitval na die deur die Duitse gebied ingestorm” is not correct — better: “het die aanvanklike verdediging deurbreek en die deur Duitse gebied ingetrek” OR more simply: “het die aanvanklike verdediging oorkom en in die deuroorheersde Duitse gebied ingestorm.” A clean suggested phrasing: “na enkele maande van intense gevegte het hulle die aanvanklike verdediging oorkom en die deur Duits- beheerste gebied binnegestorm.”
findings.translation_quote: Na ’n paar maande van intense gevegte het hulle die aanvanklike verdediging oorkom en het in die deur die Duitse gebied ingestorm.
